game: LAC @ MIA, 2025-10-12 13:00 ET, outdoor, MIA +3.5, total 45.5

script.base: LAC is a 3.5-point road favorite with implied totals LAC 24.5 and MIA 21.0 in a 45.5 game, so the book expects a one-score lead, not a blowout and not a slog. Hampton (43 carries, 242 rush yards in weeks 3-5) is the late clock back if that lead holds, while Herbert still throws enough that Allen (27 targets) and Johnston (26) stay involved. Miami does not abandon Achane (42 carries L3) but, as a 3.5 dog, tilts pass if they trail, with Waddle (21 targets, 197 yards L3) ahead of Hill (16 targets, 116 yards).
script.flip1: LAC gets up by two scores early, runs the clock, and Herbert/Allen/Johnston yards stall while Hampton's carries spike; Miami drops the run, so Achane's rush line dies and Waddle/Hill targets jump.
script.flip2: Miami hangs around or leads. Tua/MIA EPA per dropback is +0.20 when not blitzed and LAC blitzes only 26%, with DE Da'Shawn Hand out and Dupree questionable, so both teams throw, Hampton's carry share dips, and Waddle plus the LAC WRs get the overs path.

injury_fallout: LAC T Joe Alt (ankle) and T Trey Pipkins (knee) are Out and G Jamaree Salyer (knee) is Questionable, so pressure should rise, rush efficiency should fall, and quick throws should bump Hampton (18 targets, 122 rec yards L3) and TEs Gadsden (11/76) and Conklin (6/33). WR Quentin Johnston is Questionable (hamstring); if he sits, targets shift to Keenan Allen (27 L3) and Ladd McConkey (20 L3, only 91 yards). WR Derius Davis is Out (knee), a small gadget loss. MIA LB Tyrel Dodson (concussion) and S Elijah Campbell (quad) are Out, so the LB spot Hampton and the TEs attack is a backup and the deep middle is thinner if Johnston plays. LAC DE Hand is Out, DE Dupree and LB Denzel Perryman are Questionable, which lightens what Miami's offense faces. MIA C Aaron Brewer (pectoral) and CB Storm Duck (ankle) are Questionable. Source: nflverse injury report in the pack, pre-game. Final inactives about 90 minutes before kick are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone chart in the pack. Location YPA only: MIA defense left 7.19 (53 att), middle 7.08 (24), right 9.68 (59); LAC defense left 6.02 (56), middle 9.26 (31), right 4.88 (65).
matchup.pressure: Miami blitzes 40%; LAC EPA/dropback is +0.14 vs blitz and -0.05 vs none, so Herbert has been better when blitzed, but Alt and Pipkins are out so that split may not travel. LAC blitzes 26%; Miami EPA/dropback is -0.23 vs blitz and +0.20 vs none, and Hand out makes the no-blitz look Miami wants more likely.
matchup.bleeds: Miami run defense allows 5.81 YPC and 27 runs of 10+ over 5 games, plus a right-side pass bleed at 9.68 YPA and 13/147 passes of 20+. LAC run defense is tighter at 4.83 YPC and 22 runs of 10+. LAC's pass bleed is the middle (9.26 YPA on 31 throws), not the outside; 20+ passes are 12/166.
matchup.overlap: Hampton's lead-back role overlaps Miami's 5.81 YPC run defense and the vacated Dodson LB spot, and his 18 targets L3 fit an OL-injury checkdown script. LAC's pass overlap is uncharted: Allen is the target leader (196 air on 27 targets) and Johnston is the vertical (281 air on 26) into a missing safety, but Johnston is questionable and the 9.68 right-side YPA is unassigned. Waddle (210 air on 21 targets, about 10 aDOT) is Miami's volume WR into a low-blitz, lighter pass rush; the middle bleed fits a slot/TE (Waller 105 yards on 9 targets) more cleanly than Hill's outside shots into LAC's 4.88/6.02 outside YPA.

form: Hampton last4 rush 24, 70, 128, 44 and rush+rec 25, 129, 165, 70; L3 role is stable at about 14 carries and 6 targets a game, but two of those four rush+rec lines missed 70.5 and 128/165 may be one-play games. Najee Harris is a change-up (6 carries, 28 yards L3; last rush 5, 28, 28). Allen last4 rec 61, 65, 37, 58 vs 61.5, L3 160 on 27 targets. Johnston last4 71, 89, 98, 40 and is questionable. McConkey last4 48, 41, 11, 39, L3 only 91 yards on 20 targets. Achane last4 rush 30, 62, 99, 16 (L3 177 on 42, 4.2 YPC) and rush+rec 122, 84, 101, 46. Waddle last4 68, 39, 48, 110, L3 197 on 21 targets, so the 110 can inflate the average. Hill last4 40, 109, 49, 67 but L3 only 116 on 16 targets, behind Waddle. Gordon last4 rush 8, 38, 10, -2. Washington last4 2, 12, 13, 0.

pro_edge.implied_totals: LAC 24.5, MIA 21.0. Favorite = (45.5+3.5)/2 = 24.5; dog = (45.5-3.5)/2 = 21.0. Matches the precomputed PRO-EDGE INPUTS.
pro_edge.script_read: Spread 3.5 is not a blowout flag, so starter snaps should hold. Total 45.5 is moderate, not a pure volume-over or a slog-under. The 3.5 dog (MIA) throws more if trailing, so Waddle/Hill/Achane targets lean up in that flip; the leader runs late, so Hampton's carries lean up if LAC leads. Build usage from shares: Hampton 43 of 60 team RB carries in the L3 rusher lines, Waddle 21 targets vs Hill 16.
pro_edge.best_price: No two-sided price saved on any prop, including Hampton rushrec 70.5 and Waddle rec 48.5. Anchor no-vig N/A. No Pinnacle, Circa, or BetOnline number, so no book beats a sharp anchor and power-devig vs overround cannot be shown.
pro_edge.lagging: No lagging-line flag. The pack gives one nflverse spread/total and no open-to-current move, and every prop from Johnston 79.5 through Gordon 0.5 has no saved price to compare to consensus after a move.
pro_edge.sleepers: Ruled out, not IR: LAC WR Derius Davis (knee) is depth, so any shift to Allen/McConkey/Johnston is small and no line move is saved to diff. LAC T Alt and T Pipkins out are OL, not skill sleepers; they hurt Hampton's rush efficiency and can bump his receptions. LAC DE Hand out. MIA S Campbell out and LB Dodson out are defensive absences that point at Hampton and LAC pass-catchers; no same-position teammate price move is saved. Johnston, Duck, Brewer, Perryman, Dupree, and Salyer are Questionable, not out, so the sleeper check is incomplete until inactives.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Miami allows 5.81 yards per carry with 27 runs of 10+ and is without LB Tyrel Dodson, and Hampton's rush-plus-receiving line of 70.5 sits well under his weeks 3-5 combined average of about 121 (242 rush plus 122 receiving) while the rush+rec market still works if Alt and Pipkins being out cuts the run and adds checkdowns.
edge_players.must_be_true: Hampton plays a full lead-back snap share, Miami's 5.81 YPC leak shows up in a live script and not only in garbage time, and he still sees roughly 4-6 targets so 70.5 is reachable if the new tackles crater pure rush yards.
edge_players.kills_it: The tackle injuries turn this into the 25 rush+rec version of his last four, Najee Harris (6 carries, 28 yards L3) vultures the efficient touches, or LAC falls so far behind that lost carries are not replaced by checkdowns.

data_check.notes: No projection, no sims, and no Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot agree or disagree on price. model_p is the last-4 cash rate (0.50 for both), not a 3-sim probability; the 3-point edge gate cannot be run and nothing is sized. Both lines are season-median stand-ins, so a 2-of-4 split is expected and is a flag, not an automatic cut of a matchup lean. Hill under 58.5 was the other candidate (L3 116 yards on 16 targets, 38.7 a game) but was dropped: a 3.5 dog is supposed to throw more, LAC pass rush is thinned, and a lean the script module disagrees with is a drop. Allen under 61.5 (3 of last 4 under) and McConkey under 41.5 (3 of last 4 under) were dropped because Johnston is Questionable and would redistribute targets. Achane rush or rush+rec under was dropped because Perryman is Questionable and Hand/Dupree injuries point the other way. Treat any implied probability near 70% as untrustworthy; these are not that.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because the Chargers' tackle injuries were the game: Hampton ran into a stacked box behind a patchwork line, finished in the 25-yard rush+rec bin, and Najee took the only clean carries, while the 128 and 165 games were one long play that the median line had already faded. Waddle lost because the 110-yard spike was the entire case over 48.5, Brewer sat, Miami's timing routes died, and either Achane got the script or Hill took the one explosive into a Chargers outside coverage that allows only 4.88 YPA to the right. No coverage chart and no inactives were available on Sunday morning, so the overlap was a team-level guess.
slip_story: One competitive one-score story, not a shootout stack and not an under stack. LAC -3.5 and total 45.5: Hampton rush+rec over is the favorite usage leg (carries if they lead, checkdowns with the tackles out) and Waddle rec over is the dog WR1 leg if Miami trails by a score. They can win together without needing opposite scripts. Do not add Hill under, a total under, Johnston over, or any TD. Two legs, one market per player. No bet placed; no stake, prices were not saved.
